notes:
Summary: Cascade DataTrust is a European healthcare data custodian evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) to host sensitive PHI and derived embeddings. Primary drivers: strict EU data residency, HIPAA BAA for US trials, SOC 2/ISO27001 alignment for supplier risk, and customer auditability (long-term retention + SIEM integration). They want a vendor that supports customer-managed keys (BYOK/HSM), pushable audit logs to their SIEM/S3, and a private control plane with per-route cost/latency controls.

Key requirements (from security + infra):
- Data residency: All production inference in EU regions; no staging traffic to non-EU without explicit opt-in.
- KMS: Customer-managed keys required for encryption-at-rest; support for AWS KMS & CloudHSM (BYOK) and key-rotation policies.
- Audit logging: Full request/response metadata (redacted where PHI appears) exported to customer's S3 + SIEM ingest; immutable delivery and retention policy configurable (90/365/730 days).
- Compliance mapping: Need a control mapping matrix that shows how Redwood PCI/SOC2/ISO controls map to Cascade's control list and evidence artifacts.
- HIPAA/BAA: Legal requires BAA draft + technical appendix (logging, encryption, breach notification SLA).
- Network: VPC peering / PrivateLink + strict egress rules; allowlist IPs for egress to KMS endpoints.
- Segmentation: For payment-related workloads (PCI scope) they want a hardened path or tokenization to keep card data out of inference pipeline.
- Performance: latency SLOs target median token latency <200ms for chat; embeddings throughput target ~500 rps for nightly batch jobs.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-high; willing to commit to Dedicated if private control plane + compliance tradeoffs are validated.

Recent timeline (bulleted):
- 2026-01-27: Intro discovery call (AE Olivia Park + SE Ethan) — high level requirements captured.
- 2026-02-04: Security questionnaire sent (completed 80%) — questions on KMS and log export outstanding.
- 2026-02-16: Technical deep-dive with Infra (Ethan) — discussed VPC peering, PrivateLink, and KMS options. Drive diagram updated (link above).
- 2026-02-25: Legal asked for BAA draft + technical appendix — Redwood provided initial template, Cascade provided redlines 2026-03-03.
- 2026-03-03: Architecture workshop scheduled (pending final times) — target to define POC network and logging endpoints.
- 2026-03-08: Internal security asked for SOC2 mapping matrix; Redwood agreed to provide mapping showing which evidence artifacts map to which Trust Services Criteria.
- 2026-03-10: Demo of Private control plane + audit-logging UX; Cascade requested ability to push logs daily to their S3 with KMS-encrypted envelopes.

Compliance mapping notes (high level):
- SOC 2: Cascade wants a matrix that ties Redwood controls/evidence to CC6.0, CC8.0 (confidentiality), CC3.0 (risk assessment). Need Type II report or service auditor report; Redwood to provide SOC 2 complementaries and sample evidence (access logs, change management, penetration test summaries).
- ISO 27001: Need Annex A controls mapping for A.8 (asset management), A.9 (access control), A.10 (cryptography), A.12 (operations), A.14 (supplier relationships). Request: provide statement on ISMS boundary for Private deployments and available certifications for cloud partners.
- HIPAA/BAA: Technical safeguards mapping — encryption at rest/in transit, audit controls, unique user IDs via SSO/SAML, automatic logging of access to PHI. BAA appendix must include breach notification SLA (48 hours initial), and list of subprocessors.
- PCI considerations: While primary workloads are PHI, Cascade has a payments vertical; ask for guidance on isolating PCI data (tokenization, redaction, or complete exclusion from inference). Redwood recommended tokenization before sending to model and separate dedicated instances with no persistent logging of raw PAN. Need final sign-off from payments compliance team.

KMS and key management specifics discussed:
- Envelope encryption model supported; customer root key in AWS KMS (or external HSM) that wraps data keys used by Redwood internal stores.
- Audit trail: key usage logs (CloudTrail) to be forwarded to Cascade SIEM; need to ensure logs include key-ARN and subject principal.
- Rotation: support periodic rotation + ability to rewrap existing objects during maintenance window.

Audit logging and evidence delivery:
- Options discussed: S3 dump (daily), real-time Kinesis/Splunk forwarder, or managed SIEM connector. Logs will include request metadata, model version, route, and redaction flag; full request bodies for PII/PHI will be stored only when explicitly enabled and encrypted with customer keys.
- Evidence for SOC2: periodic snapshots (access logs, change logs, incident reports) + SOC2 report. Redwood will annotate which artifacts are available from hosted vs private deployments.

POC / success criteria:
- Set up Private VPC in EU with VPC peering and PrivateLink endpoints.
- Demonstrate KMS BYOK integration and ability to rotate keys without downtime in a staging window.
- Deliver logged events to Cascade S3 + SIEM with configured retention and confirm redaction rules.
- Meet latency target: median token latency <200ms for baseline chat prompts; embeddings throughput >400 rps sustained for 30 minutes.

Next actions agreed / owner tasks:
- Redwood (Ethan): prepare SOC2/ISO control mapping doc + BAA technical appendix (deliver by 2026-03-15).
- Cascade (Security): provide finalized list of required evidence and SIEM ingestion endpoint.
- Legal (both): review BAA redlines; target sign-off prior to POC start.
- Schedule architecture workshop and POC kickoff: target week of 2026-03-22.

Freeform AE notes: Good fit if we can show clear mapping for SOC2/ISO + strong BYOK story. Payments scoping adds complexity (PCI) but manageable with tokenization. Keep pressure on legal timeline — BAAs are the gating item.
